name: mio_basic
kind: installation from the version 1 / 2 readings, frozen before any replay with a changed engine or tree; no new GPU data: (M1) results of a warp's MIO producers return one per return interval, (M2) one server per SM and operation class, (M3) the in-flight group of four with the wait at issue, (M4) CS2R.CLOCK and VOTE as 2-cycle unit instructions
mechanisms: instruction.service (S2R, LDS, SHFL.BFLY, SHFL.IDX, S2UR, LDC, LDCU, CS2R.CLOCK, VOTE)
MIO queue (mio_throttle; new ledger reason mio_inflight)
why: Version 1 / 2 addenda: the producers of a run issue one cycle apart and their results come back 2 cycles apart (SHFL.IDX 4) with the wait on the reader, where the replay spaces the issues on an SMSP unit (h100) or has no spacing (b300); S2R, S2UR and resident LDC are served at 2.0 cycles per instruction per SM, LDS and SHFL.BFLY at 1.0, each kind against itself only, where the replay has no per-SM server; S2UR and LDC (and b300 LDCU) wait at issue after every four of a run, which the replay does not have; CS2R and VOTE cost 2 cycles each on the execution unit and their reader does not wait, where the replay gives CS2R 14 + 6 per instruction on h100 and VOTE a 13-cycle reader wait.
data_seen_before_freezing: mio_basic v1 / v2 addenda and tables ($CYCLESCOPE_ARTIFACT_ROOT/stall-attribution/mio_basic-readings/{T-table.txt, T-table-v2.txt, read-*.txt}); the replays of build 68702860 in mio_basic-r3, mio_basic-v2, mio_basic-v2w32. No replay with a changed engine or tree.

(a) One warp, T(n) (v1 / v2 quantity). With first latency L and results 2 apart behind producers issued 1 apart, T = L + n - 2 (SHFL.IDX, 4 apart: L + 3 n - 4). h100 clock T at n = 4 / 8 / 16: S2R 25 / 29 / 37 (L 23), LDS 25 / 29 / 37 (23), SHFL.BFLY 26 / 30 / 38 (24), SHFL.IDX 34 / 46 / 70 (26); b300 samples give the same within 1.5 (its one-warp clock carries a constant of 8.6). The installed leaves give S2R 23, SHFL.BFLY 24, SHFL.IDX 26, S2UR 35 on both devices and LDS 2 + 21 (h100) / 1 + 21 (b300) = storage.shared.issue cycles + result latency after the engine's truncation: no latency leaf needs a new value.

(b) S2UR and resident LDC, one warp: mio_throttle on the producers per iteration at n = 4 / 6 / 8 / 10 / 12 / 16 is 0 / 4 / 4 / 8 / 8 / 12 on both devices; b300 LDCU 0 / 4 / 12 at n = 4 / 8 / 16 (v1 table: the same signature; LDCU was left out of the v2 summary because its several-warp behaviour is open). The fifth producer of a run issues 8 cycles after the first = when the turn of the fourth (start 6, 2 long) has ended; the sixth to eighth follow one cycle apart. A count of instructions in flight that frees an entry when its own turn ends does not give this (at cycle 4 only two turns are unfinished); a group that is released as a whole does. Hand model of M1 + M3 against hardware T, n = 4 / 6 / 8 / 10 / 12 / 16: S2UR (L 35) 37 / 39 / 41 / 43 / 45 / 49 against h100 36.6 / 39.3 / 41.7 / 43.9 / 47.2 / 55.6 and b300 37.4 / 40.0 / 42.8 / 46.5 / 48.6 / 56.8: the hardware reader waits 2 (n = 12) to 7 (n = 16) cycles more than the rule gives, cause unknown; n = 12 and 16 are therefore reported, not judged, in K1. Resident LDC: hardware T = L + 2 + 4 (ceil(n / 4) - 1) for multiples of four with L = 26.1 (h100 clock 28.1 / 32.1 / 40.2; n = 6 / 10 / 12: 30.1 / 33.8 / 36.4 against 30 / 34 / 36), b300 the same within 1.6 except n = 4 (31.6). b300 LDCU: L = 15.2 (17.3 / 21.9 / 29.4).

(c) The constant paths' re-read latency (memory.constant_cache vector_reread_cycles 22.75 / 27.5, uniform_reread_cycles 19.0 on b300; constant_paths v1, measured as the reader's wait in that protocol's cells at several warps per SM) differs from the first latency of the one-warp runs here (LDC 26.1 on both, LDCU 15.2). This protocol does not change those leaves: with them the hand model gives h100 LDC T 3 below the hardware at every n, b300 LDC about 1.5 above (n = 4: 1.6 below), b300 LDCU about 3.6 above. The LDC / LDCU cells are judged on the wait at issue (K3) and their T is reported.

(d) Mixed runs, one warp (4 + 4 alternating), hardware T h100 / b300: S2R + LDS 28.5 / 29.9 and LDS + SHFL.BFLY 28.9 / 30.2 = one chain of eight results 2 apart (hand model 29 / 28 and 30 / 30; independent chains would give 21 and 22); S2R + S2UR 33.6 / 33.2 and LDC + S2R 24.9 / 25.5 = independent chains (hand model 34 and, with the constant leaves of (c), 22 / 26; one chain would give 40 and 32). Hence the chains: S2R, LDS, SHFL together; LDC alone; S2UR alone. LDCU alone and SHFL.IDX in the chain of SHFL.BFLY are assumptions (LDCU and SHFL.IDX were only measured in runs of their own kind).

(e) Per SM (v2): periods of the saturated cells equal producers per SM per iteration x 2.0 (S2R 8 x 16 and 16 x 32, S2UR 8 x 16, LDC 8 x 16) or x 1.0 (LDS and SHFL.BFLY 16 x 16 and 16 x 32); mixed runs of two kinds at 16 warps do not saturate. The split of the wait between producers (mio_throttle) and reader at saturation depends on the order in which the SM serves the warps, which is not measured: hardware S2UR 8 x 16 has 69 / 74 per iteration on the producers, LDC 71 / 74, S2R 22 / 24 (S2R shows no wait at issue up to 24 per warp at one warp; the bound that appears at 16 warps is not identified and not installed), LDS 16 x 16 84 and SHFL.BFLY similar (bound not identified, not installed). The earlier service_latency reading of 3.99 cycles per SHFL per SMSP at one warp per SMSP (source service_latency.<device>.v3r4, four SMSPs loaded) is the same rate as 1.0 per SM; for SHFL.UP / .DOWN / .IDX that reading is all there is (no mio_basic cell saturates them) and their leaves keep it, except that SHFL.IDX's spacing moves to the return chain (M1).

(f) CS2R.32 of SR_CLOCKLO (operation class CS2R.CLOCK) and VOTE.ANY (class VOTE): T = n on both devices (clock 1 / 4 / 8 / 16), math_pipe_throttle n - 1 over the producers and 1 on the reader (an IADD3, unit alu_smsp), no scoreboard wait: every producer and the reader take turns on one unit 2 cycles apart. The other CS2R classes (GLOBALTIMER, ZERO) and VOTEU were not measured and are not changed.

rules.fields: New fields of the instruction.service leaf (schema instruction_template; absent or 0 = the rule does not apply and timing is bit for bit as before): return_interval_cycles (float64, cycles), return_chain (uint64, enum, 1-7), sm_service_interval_cycles (float64, cycles), warp_inflight_group (uint64, count).
rules.turn: An instance whose leaf has return_interval_cycles r > 0 or sm_service_interval_cycles q > 0 takes a turn when it issues. Issue itself is not delayed by M1 or M2. turn_start = max(issue cycle, chain_free of its warp and chain (if r > 0), server_free of its SM and operation class (if q > 0)); then chain_free = turn_start + r and server_free = turn_start + q. Turns are taken in issue order. The three times are kept as fractions; a whole-cycle view takes the ceiling. No turn: a predicated-off instance; an instance whose access is remote shared memory (its timing stays as today).
rules.M1: Per warp and return_chain one chain_free. Every term of the instance's result that counts from its issue cycle today counts from turn_start: the service result latency; for LDS the storage.shared.issue row (result = turn_start + the row's cycles + completion latency; an instance that takes a turn neither reads nor advances the row's per-SMSP frontier, and its read barrier is released at turn_start as it is at the row's start today); for LDC / LDCU the re-read term of constant_paths C2 (line resident and filled: ready at turn_start + reread; fill in flight: max(turn_start + reread, fill ready); line not resident: unchanged, the fill starts at issue). Chains: 1 = S2R, LDS, SHFL.BFLY, SHFL.IDX; 2 = LDC; 3 = S2UR; 4 = LDCU (b300).
rules.M2: Per SM and operation class one server_free (S2R, S2UR, LDC: q = 2.0; LDS, SHFL.BFLY: q = 1.0). Classes do not queue behind each other.
rules.M3: Per warp and chain a count. Whenever the chain is idle (current cycle >= chain_free) the count is 0. An instance whose leaf has warp_inflight_group g > 0 cannot issue while the count is >= g and the current cycle < chain_free: it waits at issue until chain_free (ledger reason mio_inflight, mapped to mio_throttle), at which cycle the count is 0. Each issue of an instance with g > 0 adds 1. g = 4 for S2UR, LDC and b300 LDCU.
rules.M4: Leaves only: CS2R.CLOCK and VOTE take 2.0 cycles of the unit alu_smsp (VOTE moves there from shfl_smsp; common/class_resource.json follows) and their result latency is 2, so a reader behind the unit turn does not wait on the scoreboard.

leaves.S2R: issue_interval_cycles 0 (h100 was 2; b300 is 0), return_interval_cycles 2.0, return_chain 1, sm_service_interval_cycles 2.0; result latency unchanged (23).
leaves.LDS: return_interval_cycles 2.0, return_chain 1, sm_service_interval_cycles 1.0; result latency and the storage.shared.issue leaf unchanged.
leaves.SHFL.BFLY: issue_interval_cycles 0 (was 3.99 / 3.99), return_interval_cycles 2.0, return_chain 1, sm_service_interval_cycles 1.0; result latency unchanged (24).
leaves.SHFL.IDX: issue_interval_cycles 0 (was 4.0 / 3.99), return_interval_cycles 4.0, return_chain 1; result latency unchanged (26.0).
leaves.S2UR: issue_interval_cycles 0 (h100 was 2), return_interval_cycles 2.0, return_chain 3, sm_service_interval_cycles 2.0, warp_inflight_group 4; result latency unchanged (35).
leaves.LDC: return_interval_cycles 2.0, return_chain 2, sm_service_interval_cycles 2.0, warp_inflight_group 4; memory.constant_cache unchanged.
leaves.LDCU (b300 only): return_interval_cycles 2.0, return_chain 4, warp_inflight_group 4; memory.constant_cache unchanged. The h100 leaf is not changed (sm_90a emits ULDC, a fixed-latency instruction whose reader never waits).
leaves.CS2R.CLOCK: result_latency_cycles = completion_latency_cycles = 2 (h100 was 14, b300 placeholder 1), issue_interval_cycles 2.0 (was 6.0 / 0), resource alu_smsp (unchanged).
leaves.VOTE: result_latency_cycles = completion_latency_cycles = 2 (was 13), issue_interval_cycles 2.0 (was 2.0 / 2.03), resource alu_smsp (was shfl_smsp).

Verdicts by tools/microbench/mio_basic/judge_v3.py. Quantities as in versions 1 / 2: extended total = sum over the loop-body pcs and the pc behind the last one, per iteration (hardware = scaled samples of every class, mean of the passes with at least 1500 samples; replay = every ledger reason / warps); T = extended total - extended total of m.nop of the same shape + 3 (n + 1), n = producers per iteration; producer rows = the loop rows whose instruction is one of the producers, reader row = the row behind the last producer; per execution = per-iteration value / the replay's issue count at that pc.

decision: Per device. All of K1-K5 pass: M1-M4 stay installed on that device. A criterion fails because the engine does not do what the rule text says: the implementation is corrected, the build and the replay are repeated, and the addenda say so. A criterion fails although the engine does what the rule says: the rule it judges is taken out on that device by removing its leaf fields (K1 or K2: M1 and M2 together with M3, the earlier leaves restored; K3: warp_inflight_group; K4: the CS2R.CLOCK / VOTE leaves restored), the rest is judged again, and the failure is written down with its numbers. K5 (i) or (iii) failing with K1-K4 passing: nothing stays installed on that device until the cause is read from the per-cell table and written down. Criteria are not changed after the first replay.
hypotheses_full_gpu: Stated before the run, not criteria: the hardware's mio_throttle that the replay lacks (H100 loop -2.4 points of residency in full-bb2b) is partly taken up by mio_inflight; short_scoreboard (loop -1.3 / -2.3) rises where runs of LDS / S2R / LDC feed a reader; math_pipe_throttle (+2.7 / +1.8) changes little in either direction (S2R and S2UR leave the units, CS2R.CLOCK takes 2 instead of 6). Cycles may move either way and are not a criterion.
not_installed_here: A bound on S2R, LDS or SHFL in flight (appears at 16 warps and, for LDS / SHFL, from 16 per warp; depth not identified); the 2 to 7 extra cycles on the S2UR reader from 12 per run; a per-SM rate for SHFL.IDX / .UP / .DOWN; the constant paths' re-read latency at one warp (data (c)); LDCU at several warps; the same-kind / other-kind alternative of the SM pipeline; CS2R.GLOBALTIMER, CS2R.ZERO, VOTEU, R2UR.
not_allowed: No value from another machine or from the literature; no full-GPU case used to choose a rule or a value; no cell dropped after its replay is seen.

addenda.text: Commit 857a62ce alone is bit for bit neutral (12 ledgers of mio_basic-r3 identical to the 68702860 replay, mio3-neutral). K1: every judged cell passes on both devices (largest |T replay - T hardware|: h100 1.34, b300 3.54 at m.s2ur.n10 with tolerance 4.65), no unit wait on a producer row. Reported: m.s2ur.n12 / .n16 -2.2 / -6.6 (h100) and -3.6 / -7.8 (b300); m.ldc T -2.6 to -3.7 on h100 and -1.6 (n = 4), +1.1 to +2.7 on b300; b300 LDCU +3.1 to +3.7 (the constant re-read leaves, data (c)). K3: replay mio_inflight = hardware mio_throttle to the digit in all 12 (h100) / 15 (b300) cells (0 / 4 / 4 / 8 / 8 / 12); reported at 16 warps: S2UR 53.9 against 69.3 and 53.6 against 74.3, LDC 61.7 against 71.3 and 56.8 against 74.2; b300 LDCU at 4 / 8 / 16 warps 4.0 against 13.5 / 11.6 / 8.3. K4: T replay = n within 1.33 of the hardware in all eight cells per device, no barrier wait on the reader; the 16-warp cells +1.8 / +2.0 % and +1.9 / +1.8 %. K5: (i) mean error over the 83 mio_basic cells h100 0.0795 -> 0.0638 (median 0.0135 -> 0.0067), b300 0.0871 -> 0.0697 (median 0.0508 -> 0.0097); (ii) 161 cases each with a ledger; (iii) branch_basic v2 K1-K3 and sync_basic v5 C1 / C2 / C4 all pass. K2: the four 2.0-cycle cells pass (S2R 8 x 16 +0.9 / -0.0 %, S2UR +1.1 / -0.1 %, LDC +0.4 / +0.4 %, S2R 16 x 32 +1.1 / +1.0 %); the four 1.0-cycle cells FAIL: extended total replay / hardware m.lds.n16.w16 479.98 / 254.35 (+88.7 %) and 479.56 / 254.87 (+88.2 %), m.lds.n16.w32 951.76 / 502.96 (+89.2 %) and 960.42 / 500.94 (+91.7 %), m.shfl_bfly.n16.w16 480.00 / 253.08 (+89.7 %) and 479.59 / 255.44 (+87.7 %), m.shfl_bfly.n16.w32 927.51 / 503.60 (+84.2 %) and 959.99 / 500.52 (+91.8 %); before this change the h100 replay had these four within 4.4 %. Reported cells show the same excess: m.lds.n8.w16 +39.9 / +39.2 %, m.shfl_bfly.n8.w16 +39.9 / +36.7 %, m.mix.s2r_lds.n8.w16 +14.7 / +14.0 %, m.mix.lds_shfl.n8.w16 +8.3 / +7.6 %. CAUSE. The engine does what M2 says: one frontier server_free per SM and class, turn_start = max(issue, chain_free, server_free). A warp's LDS turns are 2 apart on its chain (M1) while the server needs 1.0 each; a warp that issues its run on its own moves the frontier by 2 per instruction, and the cycles between its turns lie behind the frontier where no other warp can be served: 16 warps x (15 x 2) = 480 per iteration instead of 256. The hardware period is producers x 1.0, so its server does use those cycles for other warps. For the 2.0-cycle classes the chain spacing equals the service time and no gap arises, which is why those cells pass. DECISION under the clause 'a criterion fails although the engine does what the rule says': M2 as worded here is not what the hardware does; M1-M3 are not installed by this protocol. The clause's re-judging of M4 alone was not carried out (no build with the M1-M3 fields removed was made): version 4 follows directly, changes only the wording of M2 (a server that grants the earliest free interval instead of a frontier), keeps M1, M3, M4, the leaves and the criteria K1-K5 word for word, and judges all four rules again on a new build. Nothing counts as installed until that verdict; the branch is not merged.
